lines.text: Think how frightened I was, Robert ... expecting them up-stairs every minute,—for all my brothers come here on Sunday, all together.
lines.note: Shows Elizabeth's brothers circling the secret engagement in the first days.

lines.text: Dogs pine to death sometimes—and if ever a dog loved a man, or a woman, Flush loves me.
lines.note: Her early plea for Flush to come to Italy, a thread through the whole correspondence.

lines.text: Now I will kiss you, dearest: used you to divine that at the very beginning, I have sometimes shortened the visit in order to arrive at the time of taking your hand?
lines.note: Robert's first tender taking of her hand, setting the tone of their love.

lines.text: I have lost my poor Flush—lost him!
lines.note: The sudden loss of Flush becomes a shared crisis and private joke.

lines.text: Poor Flush—how sorry I am for you, my Ba!
lines.note: Robert's sympathy for the lost dog mirrors his care for her.

lines.text: Was ever any in the world, in any possible world, so perfectly good and dear to another as you are to me!
lines.note: Elizabeth's praise of his goodness at the height of the dog-stealer dispute.

lines.text: To be parted from you so long, teaches me the necessity of your presence—I am your very, very own.
lines.note: Her admission that separation teaches her need of him, just before the wedding plan.

lines.text: Dearest, you are a prophet, I suppose—there can be no denying it.
lines.note: The sudden family removal forces the final decision to marry and leave.

lines.text: I will go for a licence to-day and we can be married on Saturday.
lines.note: Robert's decisive plan to marry on Saturday and go to Italy.

lines.text: Dearest, I write one word, and have one will which is yours.
lines.note: Elizabeth's surrender of her will to his as the elopement begins.

lines.text: Words can never tell you, however,—form them, transform them anyway,—how perfectly dear you are to me—perfectly dear to my heart and soul.
lines.note: Robert's wedding-day avowal that words cannot tell how dear she is.

lines.text: Ever dearest, I write a word that you may read it and know how all is safe so far, and that I am not slain downright with the day—oh, such a day!
lines.note: Elizabeth's breathless report that the secret wedding day is safely over.

lines.text: Is this my last letter to you, ever dearest?
lines.note: Her final letter, asking if this is the last, closes the farewell.
